answer: The opal deposit requirement creates a unique barrier to identity reservation, as this scarce resource cannot be purchased with capital. The enforcement mechanism forces each agent to pay the per-identity cost to the garden manager before any service can be provided. This system reaches its nadir when considering potential abuse, yet effectively prevents sybil attacks by making the scarce resource time, not money. The garden's security relies on this time-based scarcity model to maintain its integrity.
